about: M9 (WP9.5b, plan 7.4 'The defined cycle', AD-19): Klartext defines a cycle once and runs it where it is called. One CYCL DEF serves every call after it; M89 runs it in its own block and after every positioning block that follows, until M99 or the next definition; a cycle that acts where it is defined (the datum shift, cycle 7, written in sub-blocks) is never called and replaces nothing; a tool change ends no definition.

states.about: Rule 1: the definition stores the cycle and runs nothing.
The last line of the parameter list is still the definition.
Rule 3: M99 runs the defined cycle once, at the end of this positioning block.
A positioning block without a call runs nothing.
Rule 2: a call never ends a definition, so CYCL CALL runs the same cycle again.
Rule 5: the datum shift acts where it is defined; it is the entry of cycle 7, reached through the sub-block, and neither runs nor replaces the drilling cycle.
Rule 2: a tool change with a cycle defined is normal and changes nothing here.
Rule 4: M89 is the first call of a modal call (the cycle manual: program the first call with M89), so this block runs the cycle and the modal call is on.
Every positioning block under the modal call runs the cycle.
A block that moves no axis runs nothing; the modal call stays.
A cycle that acts where it is defined does not end the modal call (only the next machining cycle does).
Its X is a shift, not a position (axisWords: data), so the block is no positioning block.
M99 on the last position runs the cycle once and ends the modal call.
Rule 1: the next definition replaces the one before it.
The tap runs here; the F of this block is the positioning feed, not the thread pitch (that is Q239).
Rule 4: the next definition ends the modal call and replaces the tap.
CYCL CALL POS moves to its position and runs the defined cycle there.
